2609.09140.title: NOAH: Learning the Full Patient Journey. A Longitudinal Multimodal Time-Aware Model for Representation and Forecasting
2609.09140.paper_summary: The digitization of healthcare has generated vast, longitudinal, and multimodal patient records over a lifetime, yet fully exploiting these data to represent and predict patient state trajectories remains a critical challenge. Current AI models often struggle to capture the complex, irregular temporal dynamics and inherent stochasticity of real-world multimodal patient data. Existing AI approaches for modeling longitudinal patient records are predominantly discriminative, limited to a few modalities, constrained by closed categorical vocabularies, treating time as a monotonic inductive bias, or they are limited in forecasting future patient states. We introduce NOAH, a time-aware, task-agnostic, generative transformer model representing and forecasting the full multimodal patient journey. NOAH features a novel bidirectional time integration and a variational latent space to capture the continuous evolution of patient states and the stochasticity of clinical trajectories. Built from over 559 million clinical events from 431,000 hospital visits of 299,000 patients across the MIMIC dataset family, NOAH natively processes medical images, time-series and numeric signals, categorical events, as well as structured and unstructured clinical records. NOAH is the first truly holistic generative model in its field, enabling autoregressive forecasting with optional time control, zero-shot classification, and counterfactual intervention simulation. It generates highly informative and predictive patient state representations that demonstrate strong performance in probing for clinical outcomes, 15 ICD chapters, and 29 comorbidities, as well as in time-to-event prediction. Seamlessly handling diverse modalities and complex temporal dynamics, NOAH provides a versatile, task-agnostic, scalable foundation for intelligent predictive systems in personalized clinical care and digital medicine.
2609.09140.paper_summary_zh: 醫療數位化產生了龐大的、長期的、多模態的病人記錄，然而充分利用這些數據來表示和預測病人狀態的軌跡仍然是一個關鍵挑戰。當前的人工智慧模型常常難以捕捉現實世界多模態病人數據的複雜、不規則的時間動態和固有的隨機性。現有的人工智慧方法在建模長期病人記錄方面主要是區分性的，僅限於少數幾種模態，受限於封閉的類別詞彙，將時間視為單調的歸納偏見，或者在預測未來病人狀態方面受到限制。我們介紹了NOAH，一種時間感知、任務無關的生成Transformer模型，能夠表示和預測完整的多模態病人旅程。NOAH具有新穎的雙向時間整合和變分潛在空間，以捕捉病人狀態的持續演變和臨床軌跡的隨機性。NOAH基於來自MIMIC數據集家族的299,000名病人的431,000次醫院就診中的超過5.59億個臨床事件構建，原生處理醫療影像、時間序列和數值信號、類別事件，以及結構化和非結構化的臨床記錄。NOAH是其領域中首個真正全面的生成模型，實現了自回歸預測，並具備可選的時間控制、零樣本分類和反事實干預模擬。它生成高度信息豐富且具預測性的病人狀態表示，在臨床結果、15個ICD章節和29種共病的探測，以及事件發生時間預測方面表現出色。NOAH無縫處理多樣的模態和複雜的時間動態，為個性化臨床護理和數位醫療中的智能預測系統提供了一個多功能、任務無關、可擴展的基礎。
